'''Jeremy Avigad''' is a professor of philosophy and a professor of mathematical sciences at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].

He received a B.A. in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 1989, and a Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of California at Berkeley]] in 1995 under the supervision of [[Jack Silver]].<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=32558 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>  He has contributed to the areas of [[mathematical logic]] and [[Foundations of mathematics|foundations]], [[formal verification]] and [[proof assistant|interactive theorem proving]], and the [[Philosophy of mathematics|philosophy]] and [[history of mathematics]].<ref>[https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/ Jeremy Avigad's official website] at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]</ref> He became Director of the Hoskinson Center for Formal Mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] after cryptocurrency entrepreneur [[Charles Hoskinson]] donated $20 million in September 2021 to establish it.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=September 2021 |title=Carnegie Mellon Receives $20 Million to Establish Hoskinson Center for Formal Mathematics in Dietrich College |work= Carnegie Mellon University |url=https://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2021/september/hoskinson-center-for-formal-mathematics.html|access-date=2021-09-27 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Siobhan |date=2 July 2023 |title=AI Is coming for mathematics, too |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/02/science/ai-mathematics-machine-learning.html |access-date=26 March 2024 |work=New York Times|quote=...said Dr. Avigad, who is the director of the Hoskinson Center for Formal Mathematics (funded by the crypto entrepreneur Charles Hoskinson)...}}</ref>
